key_insight: Turbulence in a T-shaped mixer develops in two stages: a near-junction jet-like transitional regime followed by a downstream decay region with power-law relaxation of velocity, dissipation, and scalar variance.
engineering_relevance: These results help predict mixing performance and mixing-length requirements in T-mixers, which is useful for designing compact chemical processing and microfluidic systems.
method: Direct numerical simulations of the turbulent regime in a T-shaped mixer
Reynolds numbers up to Re = 2000 at Schmidt number Sc = 1
Streamwise analysis of velocity, turbulence, and scalar mixing evolution
evidence_signal: The study uses DNS data to identify two distinct streamwise stages and compares observed decay exponents with known turbulence scalings, while also fitting time-averaged scalar profiles with an effective diffusion coefficient.
watch_item: The conclusions are established for Sc = 1 and Re up to 2000, so extrapolation to other fluids, higher Reynolds numbers, or different channel geometries should be done cautiously.
paper_title: Stages of turbulence generation and decay in a T-shaped mixer
